questions.stem: What proportion of neonates with oesophageal atresia also have a tracheo-oesophageal fistula?
How common is tracheo-oesophageal fistula at birth?
Pure oesophageal atresia with no fistula is which Gross type?
Which Gross type is the most common, with a distal fistula into the trachea?
Gross D tracheo-oesophageal fistula is oesophageal atresia with a ____ TOF.
questions.answer: double

questions.stem: Which Gross type is H-type fistula without oesophageal atresia?
What does the prognosis of tracheo-oesophageal fistula depend on?
questions.answer: Weight and associated cardiac problems

questions.stem: When is tracheo-oesophageal fistula usually diagnosed now?
options: In the first year of life

questions.stem: What is the classic presentation of tracheo-oesophageal fistula within hours of birth?
What are the three Cs of late tracheo-oesophageal fistula presentation, especially with feeds?
questions.answer: Choking, coughing and cyanosis

questions.stem: Which ongoing respiratory problems does tracheo-oesophageal fistula cause?
questions.answer: Aspiration risk, pneumonitis and recurrent chest infections

questions.stem: Why does abdominal distension occur in tracheo-oesophageal fistula?
questions.answer: Gas enters the stomach through the fistula

questions.stem: In oesophageal atresia, where does a nasogastric tube coil on chest X-ray?
What problems can persist after tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair?
questions.answer: Reflux, oesophageal stricture or tracheomalacia

questions.stem: What does VATER stand for in the associations of tracheo-oesophageal fistula?
questions.answer: Vertebral, anal, tracheo-oesophageal, radial or renal

questions.stem: What does VACTERL stand for in the associations of tracheo-oesophageal fistula?
questions.answer: Vertebral, anorectal, cardiovascular, tracheo-oesophageal, renal, limb

questions.stem: What ventilation should be avoided in a neonate with tracheo-oesophageal fistula before repair?
questions.answer: Positive pressure ventilation

questions.stem: Initial IV fluids for a neonate with tracheo-oesophageal fistula should contain ____.
questions.answer: glucose

questions.stem: How should a neonate with tracheo-oesophageal fistula be nursed during initial stabilisation?
questions.answer: Head up

questions.stem: What tube, on what suction, is used during initial stabilisation for tracheo-oesophageal fistula?
questions.answer: Replogle tube on continuous low-pressure suction

questions.stem: When must a tracheo-oesophageal fistula be closed?
questions.answer: Soon after birth

questions.stem: Which approach is usually used for tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair?
options: Right thoracotomy in the lateral position

questions.stem: What may be done first to locate the fistula in tracheo-oesophageal fistula surgery?
questions.answer: Bronchoscopy

questions.stem: In primary repair of tracheo-oesophageal fistula, what happens at fistula closure?
questions.answer: The oesophageal ends are sewn together

questions.stem: In long-gap oesophageal atresia, when is the gastrostomy placed?
How are post-repair oesophageal strictures and dysmotility assessed and treated?
questions.answer: Contrast studies and balloon dilatation

questions.stem: Which preoperative test assesses cardiac anomalies in tracheo-oesophageal fistula?
questions.answer: Echocardiography

questions.stem: Why might limb anomalies matter for tracheo-oesophageal fistula anaesthesia?
questions.answer: They may make venous and arterial access difficult

questions.stem: Which preoperative blood tests are needed before tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair?
questions.answer: Routine bloods, especially electrolytes, plus group and crossmatch

questions.stem: In tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair, how is the upper pouch managed to prevent regurgitation?
questions.answer: Aspirate it via the Replogle; leave in or remove as the surgeon prefers

questions.stem: Why is an invasive arterial line used during tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair?
questions.answer: For metabolic monitoring and to detect surgical compression of great vessels

questions.stem: In tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair, what is the main concern when ventilating the patient?
options: Pneumothorax from high peak airway pressure
Gastric distension from ventilation through the fistula

questions.stem: In tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair, how is ventilation handled until the fistula is ligated?
questions.answer: Keep spontaneous ventilation, or give gentle low-pressure mask ventilation

questions.stem: Which surgical approach is usually used for tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair?
In tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair, when is a needle gastrostomy needed?
questions.answer: Rarely, to decompress the stomach before the fistula is tied

questions.stem: After tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair, the child usually returns to ICU for a period of ____.
questions.answer: IPPV

questions.stem: After tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair, what neck position reduces anastomotic tension?
options: Head turned fully to one side

questions.stem: What is the reported anastomotic leak rate after tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair?
After tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair, what share of children need dilatation for oesophageal stricture?
What rate of stridor and tracheomalacia is reported after tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair?
After tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair, how is reflux treated?
questions.answer: Antacids first, with fundoplication later if needed

questions.stem: Which respiratory problems can complicate tracheo-oesophageal fistula repair?
questions.answer: Aspiration, atelectasis, recurrent pneumonia and respiratory infections
